_comment: Anchor/positive/negative triplets for the embedding-quality eval, keyed by the sample document each was written against. Synthetic: both source documents are written for this repository, so nothing here is real user content. The positive is a paraphrase that deliberately shares few words with the anchor, so lexical overlap cannot carry it. Each negative shares the anchor's vocabulary but not its meaning: hard_negative_kind is 'inversion' when it reverses the anchor's claim in near-identical wording, and 'adjacent_fact' when it states a different, neighbouring fact from the same document. easy_negative is a sentence from elsewhere in the corpus, on a different subject.

sample.txt.anchor: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds a language model in an external knowledge base so that answers can cite real source material.
sample.txt.positive: Tying the model to outside documents lets it point at where each statement came from instead of inventing it.
sample.txt.hard_negative: A language model relying solely on parametric memory cites no external knowledge base and grounds its answers in no real source material.
sample.txt.easy_negative: Each document carries an access role, and every search is filtered by it.

sample.txt.anchor: Chunks that are too large dilute the signal and waste the context window.
sample.txt.positive: Oversized passages bury what matters among filler and burn through the space the model has to read.
sample.txt.hard_negative: Chunks that are too small fracture ideas across boundaries and lose the surrounding meaning a reader needs.
sample.txt.easy_negative: Extraction turns a binary document into plain text the rest of the pipeline can work with.

sample.txt.anchor: Fixed-size chunking slices the text stream into windows of a set length, ignoring sentence and section boundaries.
sample.txt.positive: The simplest splitter counts off equal spans and pays no attention to where sentences or headings fall.
sample.txt.hard_negative: A structure-aware splitter follows the boundaries a document already marks rather than slicing the text stream into windows of a set length.
sample.txt.easy_negative: A file that is not a readable document is rejected outright instead of being silently stored as empty text.

sample.txt.anchor: The virtue of fixed-size chunking is predictability: every chunk except the last has exactly the same size.
sample.txt.positive: You know in advance how big each piece will be, which makes throughput easy to reason about.
sample.txt.hard_negative: The weakness of fixed-size chunking is that every chunk except the last cuts through the middle of a sentence.
sample.txt.easy_negative: Chunks are written one at a time as they are produced, so a large document never holds all of its chunks in memory.

sample.txt.anchor: Fixed-size chunking cuts through the middle of sentences and can strand an important clause at the edge of a chunk.
sample.txt.positive: Slicing blindly leaves half an idea dangling where the retriever is unlikely to surface it whole.
sample.txt.hard_negative: Fixed-size chunking never cuts through the middle of a sentence, so no clause is ever stranded at the edge of a chunk.
sample.txt.easy_negative: Recall is the share of the passages that should have been retrieved for a question that actually were.

sample.txt.anchor: A typical pipeline ingests documents, splits them into retrievable chunks, embeds each chunk into a vector, and stores those vectors for similarity search.
sample.txt.positive: Text comes in, gets broken into pieces, each piece is turned into numbers, and the numbers are kept where they can be looked up by closeness.
sample.txt.hard_negative: A typical pipeline ingests documents and stores them whole, splitting them into no chunks and embedding no vectors for similarity search.
sample.txt.easy_negative: Exclusion blanks a page rather than dropping it, so the pages that follow retain their original numbers.

sample.txt.anchor: Because it is so simple, fixed-size chunking makes an honest baseline.
sample.txt.positive: Being the least clever option is exactly what makes it the right thing to measure everything else against.
sample.txt.hard_negative: Fixed-size chunking is too simple to serve as an honest baseline, so cleverer strategies are compared against each other instead.
sample.txt.easy_negative: The text of each page is kept separately so that every downstream chunk can still say which page it came from.

sample.txt.anchor: The way a document is divided determines what the retriever can find and how much irrelevant context it drags along.
sample.txt.positive: Where you place the cuts decides both what turns up in a search and how much noise comes with it.
sample.txt.hard_negative: What the retriever can find is determined by the embedding model, not by the way a document is divided.
sample.txt.easy_negative: Encrypted files, truncated downloads and files that merely claim to be PDFs all fail here.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: Exclusion blanks a page rather than dropping it, so the pages that follow retain their original numbers.
structured_sample.txt.positive: A skipped page is emptied in place, which means nothing after it has to be renumbered.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: Exclusion drops a page rather than blanking it, so the pages that follow lose their original numbers.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: The semantic strategy embeds each sentence and breaks where consecutive sentences drift apart in meaning.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: Because exclusion happens before chunking, it behaves identically for every chunking strategy.
structured_sample.txt.positive: Running it first means no splitter can see the removed material, whichever splitter is used.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: Because exclusion happens after chunking, it behaves differently for every chunking strategy.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: A chunk is a contiguous span of text treated as one retrievable unit.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: A file that is not a readable document is rejected outright instead of being silently stored as empty text.
structured_sample.txt.positive: Anything that cannot actually be opened is turned away at the door rather than let through holding nothing.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: A file that is not a readable document is silently stored as empty text instead of being rejected outright.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: Every chunk is embedded into a fixed-length vector and written to the store.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: A structure-aware strategy looks for the markers a document already carries: headings, numbered sections, labelled clauses.
structured_sample.txt.positive: It splits where the author has already said that one part ends and the next begins.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: A structure-aware strategy ignores the markers a document already carries and counts off a set number of words instead.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: Each document carries an access role, and every search is filtered by it.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: The semantic strategy embeds each sentence and breaks where consecutive sentences drift apart in meaning.
structured_sample.txt.positive: It watches for the point where the subject changes and cuts there, going by the vectors rather than the layout.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: The semantic strategy embeds each sentence and breaks where consecutive sentences are closest in meaning.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: Pages that carry no useful text, such as scanned covers or blank separators, are excluded before anything else runs.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: Chunks are written one at a time as they are produced, so a large document never holds all of its chunks in memory.
structured_sample.txt.positive: Each piece goes to the store the moment it exists, which keeps the memory cost flat however long the input is.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: Chunks are collected and written in a single batch at the end, so a large document holds all of its chunks in memory.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: Its virtue is predictability, and that makes it an honest baseline for anything more clever to beat.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: A chunk is only ever returned to a caller whose role matches the document it belongs to, so access is enforced in the query.
structured_sample.txt.positive: The permission check happens while the search runs, so material the reader may not see never comes back at all.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: A chunk is returned to any caller and the role is checked after the results come back, rather than in the query.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: Extraction turns a binary document into plain text the rest of the pipeline can work with.

structured_sample.txt.anchor: An embedding is the vector a model produces for a span of text, positioned so that related spans sit close together.
structured_sample.txt.positive: Turning words into coordinates puts things that mean similar things near one another.
structured_sample.txt.hard_negative: An embedding is the vector a model produces for a span of text, positioned so that related spans sit far apart.
structured_sample.txt.easy_negative: Its virtue is predictability: every chunk except the last has exactly the same size.
